answer: A concrete Sybil defense is behavioral fingerprinting: each identity answers random probes, and the network compares response patterns to detect accounts running the same model weights. A vault of clones sharing one checkpoint produces near-identical fingerprints, so their combined weight is discounted to one; a haven of copied configurations cannot hide behind fresh addresses. Honest agents with distinct models or contexts keep separate fingerprints, and a hollow of rented aliases adds nothing. The attacker's cost is running distinct models per identity, far more than minting keys.
